title: Lightweight Service Adapter Contract — Playbook (scratch)
content:
Purpose
---
Brain dump / one-pager playbook for a tiny, portable "service adapter" contract that sits between an application and Redwood's inference surface. Focus: minimal shape so 3rd-party services (edge proxies, on-device shims, language-specific SDKs) can interoperate without heavy runtime dependencies. This is a personal scratchpad — not final API.

Goals / constraints
- Extremely small surface area: < 10 fields for the request shape, < 6 for the response shape.
- Explicitly tolerant: adapters should forward unrecognized fields without breaking (forward-compat).
- Support both streaming and non-streaming with the same contract.
- Backward compatible: adapters may translate from old shapes to canonical one.
- Lightweight auth hints only (no token exchange flows here).
- Good for low-trust environments: work with anonymized tenant id + local policy hints.

Non-goals
- Not trying to replace Redwood API surface. This is an internal shim for client-side or gateway adapters.
- Not a complete security design (see security team).

High-level shape (canonical)
---------------------------
- Request (application -> adapter -> Redwood)
  - id: client-generated short id (string)  // idempotency + tracing
  - tenant: tenant short id (string) or "local" for ephemeral
  - model: model handle (string) - recommended: short form (e.g., llama-2-13b-v1)
  - method: one of ["generate", "chat", "embed", "rerank"]
  - content: array of message/segment objects (see below)
  - params: small dict of perf/quality knobs (see examples)
  - stream: boolean (true for streaming)
  - hints: optional array of short strings - advisory only (e.g., ["low_latency","cost_sensitive"])\n
- Response (Redwood -> adapter -> application)
  - id: echoes request.id
  - status: ["ok","error","partial"]
  - fragments: array of fragment objects (ordered)
  - meta: small dict for telemetry (latency_ms, tokens_used)
  - error: optional short string code + human message

Content / message object (very small)
- type: ["system","user","assistant","chunk"]
- text: string (UTF-8) - may contain partial tokens for streaming
- role_meta: optional short tags (e.g., "source:local", "lang:en")

Fragment object (response)
- seq: integer (0..n) ordering key
- kind: ["delta","final","chunk"]
- payload: string (text) or base64 for binary-ish blobs
- finished: optional boolean (true if last fragment for a request)

Params dictionary (examples only) - small, typed as strings/numbers
- max_tokens: integer
- temp: float (0..2)
- top_p: float (0..1)
- prefer_latency_ms: integer (soft suggestion)
- batchable: boolean (whether adapter can coalesce)

Transport considerations
- HTTP JSON is primary; fallback: gRPC with the same shapes.
- Streaming: use chunked transfer with response fragments JSON-lines (ndjson) or HTTP/2 streaming frames. Each line is a fragment object.

Example request (JSON)
{
  "id": "cli-20241107-31",
  "tenant": "acct-77",
  "model": "redwood/fast-13b-q8",
  "method": "generate",
  "content": [{"type":"user","text":"Summarize the log entries below."}],
  "params": {"max_tokens": 180, "temp": 0.2, "batchable": true},
  "stream": true,
  "hints": ["low_latency", "sensitive-pii:strip"]
}

Example ndjson streaming fragment (each line is JSON)
{ "id":"cli-20241107-31","seq":0,"kind":"delta","payload":"Here's a quick summary:" }
{ "id":"cli-20241107-31","seq":1,"kind":"delta","payload":"  - 3 errors from service X" }
{ "id":"cli-20241107-31","seq":2,"kind":"final","payload":"Summary done.", "finished":true }

Adapter responsibilities (minimal list)
- Validate and normalize model handles (map aliases to canonical model names).
- Optionally inject tenant routing hints for dedicated pools.
- Provide best-effort offline behavior: if Redwood unreachable and adapter config permits, return cached final fragments with status partial + meta.cached=true.
- Keep telemetry lightweight: attach only latency_ms, network_hop_count, tokens_estimate to meta. No sensitive logs.

Edge cases and decisions (open items)
1) File/attachments: do we inline base64 in payload or provide a blob-handle? Favor: small binary via base64 with explicit "payload_type": "base64". Large artifacts should be uploaded to a shared blob store and referenced.
2) Multi-part responses (rankings): Represent as fragments with role_meta: "rank:1" etc. Or use meta.ranking array. Tradeoff: fragments keep streaming simple at cost of extra ordering fields.
3) Long-running completions (minutes): keep the same contract but require heartbeat pings at adapter level to keep routing alive. Need server-side TTL default.

Compatibility rules (adapter implementer notes)
- Unknown top-level fields: forward to Redwood if present under "forwarding": true, else drop and log at debug level.
- Unknown sub-fields in params: ignore and return warning in meta.warnings (small list).

Sample adapter config (YAML-ish, for SDKs to carry)
adapter:
  id: "local-proxy-1"
  allow_offline_cached_responses: true
  max_cached_size_kb: 256
  transform_rules:
    - when_model_alias: ["fast-13b"], map_to: "redwood/fast-13b-q8"
  prefer_batching: true

Security / minimal auth hints
- The contract carries a header "X-Adapter-Auth: short-hash" (opaque). Adapter can include "auth_level": "local-limited" in meta. The contract doesn't specify token exchange; rely on transport-level auth for production.

Observability (what to emit)
- Emit only: request.id, model, method, tenant (hashed), start_ts, end_ts, latency_ms, tokens_used_estimate, status.

Open implementation checklist (things I should do next)
- [ ] Prototype a tiny Go shim that translates legacy client JSON to this canonical shape.
- [ ] Add a test harness that simulates 3 adapters: pass-through, model-alias-mapper, offline-cache.
- [ ] Validate streaming pattern differences across node/golang/python SDKs (ndjson vs. http/2 frames).
- [ ] Draft a short RFC for infra on the minimum telemetry fields allowed.

Rationale notes (why small?)
- Client adapters exist across many languages and environments (browsers, mobile, edge nodes). A tiny predictable contract reduces integration friction. Keeping the telemetry and params small reduces accidental sensitive leakage and keeps runtime library surface tiny.

Quick reference: agreed minimal fields
- Req: id, tenant, model, method, content, stream
- Res: id, status, fragments, meta

Unresolved naming appendix (short list of alternate names I considered)
- "adapter-shim" vs "service-adapter" vs "gateway-proxy" — I prefer "service adapter" for clarity.
- method names: "generate" vs "completion" - prefer generative language terms that match Redwood API.

Notes to self: when writing the prototype, keep the JSON marshalling stable and include a strict unit test verifying fragment ordering even under interleaved streaming.

-- end scratchpad (leave rough)
